title: Primordial Paradox TALK cards
description: The shipping TALK personality cards, one per enemy per phase, per specs/16-talk-command.md section 10. Data only: no GML module ever tests an enemy name. A card's enemy must be an enemy id in data/enemies/roster.json, and every enemy in data/enemies/all.json must have a card here; that cross reference is a job for tools/check_talk.py (spec section 15 check 5), because a schema cannot read a second file. Every reply line is printable ASCII, 1 to 60 characters: 60 is two full lines at 30 characters (spec 05), so a checked reply can never overflow the message box. The navy_sailor and percy cards carry the approved cards from spec section 10 word for word, so the decided spec and the shipping data cannot drift.

rule.description: One line naming the spec and the content source, the way data/enemies/roster.json carries its rule line.

cards.description: One card per enemy per phase. The base card for an enemy has an empty phase.

line.description: One reply_line: printable ASCII only, no leading or trailing space, 60 characters at most. The box draws it as '* ' plus this text (spec 05), so the asterisk is not part of the line.

items.description: Lowercase only (spec section 15 check 5). A hit is a keyword appearing as a whole word, or a two word phrase appearing as a substring (spec section 9 step 2).

bucketLineList.description: The lines for one mercy bucket. Two lines per bucket is legal: spec section 10's own navy_sailor card ships two, and that card is kept byte identical.

classLines.description: The lines for one class when the three mercy buckets do not differ: one array of at least 3 lines (spec section 10).

bucketedPool.description: A class pool whose low, mid and high replies differ. All three buckets are required, and each holds at least one line, so the class carries at least 3 lines in total, which is spec section 15 check 5's floor.

pools.description: Five classes, chosen by the fallback's scoring class (spec section 9 step 5). Weak and strong need buckets in the demo cards because the tone has to move with the meter; neutral, rude and cheat are one array unless a card genuinely needs buckets.

id.description: Card id. For a base card this equals enemy; for a phase card it is the phase id, so the cache key never collides (spec section 8).

enemy.description: An enemy id. Every enemy in data/enemies/all.json must resolve to a card; the six roster enemies that have no fight row yet are carded here in advance, because data/enemies/roster.json is where their voice, wants, fears and topics already live.

phase.description: Empty for the base card. A phase card names the phase, and data/enemies/all.json's phase row must name the same set, so the director never guesses (spec section 10).

version.description: Bumped on any edit. Part of the cache key (spec section 8).

voice.description: One sentence the model must match (spec section 10).

lines.description: Optional flat copy of every reply line in the pools, for a checker that wants one list. When present it must equal the union of the pool lines, which no schema can compare; tools/check_talk.py owns that rule (spec section 15 check 5). The navy_sailor card ships without it, because the spec's card is reproduced exactly.
